The live owner doc preserves every source atom listed in source_atom_ids without treating the ledger as canonical product prose.
Exact tokens, negative constraints, owner hints, and accepted corrections remain available to future audits through this PlanUnit.
The handoff schema carries the runtime-v2 PlanCompileRun fields `contract_mode`, `launch_policy`, `runtime_adapter`, `runtime_enablement_ref`, and `runtime_policy_snapshot_ref`; design_only records remain disabled, while native_runtime records require enablement evidence before automatic launch.
No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, GoalRuns, implementation files, generated governance artifacts, or production build tasks are created by this compile.
Approval creates an immutable, versioned Approved PRD Pack containing the primary PRD, accepted PRD-ledger snapshot, source manifest, traceability, assumptions and constraints, open questions, quality report, approval receipt, hashes, and version identity. Edits after approval create a new draft based on the approved version and require a new approval event; previous Approved PRD Packs remain immutable and addressable. Planning Wizard accepts an Approved PRD Pack, normalized imported requirements pack, or structured Assistant Chat handoff seed, preserving source identity, version, hashes, warnings, amendments, and lineage. PlanningRun owns source pack identity, project and work-intent context, thread group, global planning ledger, dynamic topic map, topic threads, topic plan drafts, amendments, invalidations, audit cycles, final plan pack, status, hashes, and handoff events. Planning Wizard child-thread identity uses thread_type planning_wizard plus thread_role values for intake, topic, final_integration, audit_review, and final_review, bound to Planning Run membership rather than minted as unrelated top-level thread families. The controller can add, split, merge, rename, defer, reopen, reorder, and mark topics impacted, recording the reason, source refs, dependencies, user-visible origin, and resulting invalidations. A later decision that changes a prior topic's assumptions or outputs marks affected topic drafts stale_due_to_dependency_change, stale_due_to_new_scope, or requires_recompile/requires_reaudit and propagates impact through typed topic dependencies. New information during planning becomes a planning clarification, immutable Planning Amendment, out_of_current_approved_scope item, or PRD revision request according to materiality and impact. Disabling or restricting automated testing requires a durable testing_policy_override explicitly approved by the user for exact projects, PlanUnits, WorkNodes, capability classes, reasons, risks, and reopen conditions. Affected work remains truthfully marked with an approved verification exception, such as completed_with_approved_verification_exception, and must never be represented as an automated test pass or full certification. Each testing capability family supports Auto, On, and Off: Auto discovers and selects or installs within authority; On is required and blocks or asks for authority when unavailable; Off prohibits use and installation for that capability without implying a pass. Approve And Build atomically writes the immutable pack, user approval receipt, and PlanApproved transactional-outbox event so approval cannot be committed without a recoverable downstream trigger. PlanApproved uses a deterministic idempotency key derived from project_id, pack_id, pack version, and pack hash; duplicate delivery returns the existing PlanCompileRun rather than creating another run. The runtime schema includes contract_mode, launch_policy, runtime_adapter, runtime_enablement_ref, and runtime_policy_snapshot_ref; the design_only branch preserves disabled bootstrap semantics, while the finished-product native_runtime branch defaults to automatic_after_approval through native_puppet_master_adapter with runtime enablement evidence. Each stage card defines exact inputs, outputs, algorithms, bounded units, read/write authority, required parallelism, validators, retry and repair routes, currentness behavior, terminal states, and evidence/receipt requirements. A certified WorkNodeRequest has non-empty objective, source PlanUnits and acceptance units, bounded read/write/implementation surfaces, typed dependencies, authority, model/capability routing, test binding, repository currentness, evidence requirements, idempotency, cancellation, and no unsupported or placeholder content. After Activation Decision accepts the graph, Executor materializes canonical WorkNodeRecord objects from accepted WorkNodeRequests and emits materialization receipts. WorkNodeRecord includes worknode_id, workgraph_id and revision, source_request_id, source PlanUnit and acceptance refs, objective, surfaces, typed readiness predicates, lifecycle, attempts and retries, authority, model, tests, repository/worktree/safe-point refs, evidence, currentness, cancellation, invalidation, and replan generation. Existing project_plan_node schema remains an import or compatibility contract with an explicit adapter and must not silently become the canonical runtime WorkNodeRecord. Work dispatch, change, test, retry, and completion receipts use worknode_id and attempt_id plus source_request_id and graph revision; a WorkNodeRequest reference alone is not sufficient runtime identity. The GoalRun activation and certification flow is retired by DL-478. Within the stable pm.plans_to_code_handoff.v1 schema document, plans-to-code runtime-capable v2 native_runtime records carry schema version, project, planning run, plan pack, PlanCompileRun, WorkGraph and revision, WorkNode, attempt, actor, status, revision, hashes, currentness, correlation, causation, idempotency, source, artifact, evidence, and supersession fields as applicable. Planning Wizard workflow and Auditor own AuditCycle, AuditFinding, RepairAttempt, AuditClosure, and CertificationReceipt records rather than Goal Runtime or superseded experimental workflow machinery. The final audit controller must launch multiple bounded read-only specialist agents in parallel for distinct defect families, persist assignments and results, reduce findings, run bounded repairs, and re-audit until all findings are durably closed or a true typed blocker remains. Audit findings have stable finding keys, source and artifact hashes, closure status, evidence, reason, repair attempts, and reopen conditions so unchanged closed findings become previously closed rather than recurring forever. The only permitted incomplete item is a user_approved_incomplete_item naming the exact artifact and span, reason, risk, approver, downstream disposition, expiration or reopen condition, and evidence; broad permission to leave TODOs is invalid. App Assistant Plans/Deep Plan are APR-073/074 and CV-368, separate from these Project-required PRD/PlanningRun/NamedPlan/Orchestrator records. Wizard handoff first establishes a real Project and fresh exact-version approval; no fields here become nullable to admit app work.

The handoff schema carries the runtime-v2 PlanCompileRun fields `contract_mode`, `launch_policy`, `runtime_adapter`, `runtime_enablement_ref`, and `runtime_policy_snapshot_ref`; design_only records remain disabled, while native_runtime records require enablement evidence before automatic launch.
No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, GoalRuns, implementation files, generated governance artifacts, or production build tasks are created by this compile.
Approval creates an immutable, versioned Approved PRD Pack containing the primary PRD, accepted PRD-ledger snapshot, source manifest, traceability, assumptions and constraints, open questions, quality report, approval receipt, hashes, and version identity. Edits after approval create a new draft based on the approved version and require a new approval event; previous Approved PRD Packs remain immutable and addressable. Planning Wizard accepts an Approved PRD Pack, normalized imported requirements pack, or structured Assistant Chat handoff seed, preserving source identity, version, hashes, warnings, amendments, and lineage. PlanningRun owns source pack identity, project and work-intent context, thread group, global planning ledger, dynamic topic map, topic threads, topic plan drafts, amendments, invalidations, audit cycles, final plan pack, status, hashes, and handoff events. Planning Wizard child-thread identity uses thread_type planning_wizard plus thread_role values for intake, topic, final_integration, audit_review, and final_review, bound to Planning Run membership rather than minted as unrelated top-level thread families. The controller can add, split, merge, rename, defer, reopen, reorder, and mark topics impacted, recording the reason, source refs, dependencies, user-visible origin, and resulting invalidations. A later decision that changes a prior topic's assumptions or outputs marks affected topic drafts stale_due_to_dependency_change, stale_due_to_new_scope, or requires_recompile/requires_reaudit and propagates impact through typed topic dependencies. New information during planning becomes a planning clarification, immutable Planning Amendment, out_of_current_approved_scope item, or PRD revision request according to materiality and impact. Disabling or restricting automated testing requires a durable testing_policy_override explicitly approved by the user for exact projects, PlanUnits, WorkNodes, capability classes, reasons, risks, and reopen conditions. Affected work remains truthfully marked with an approved verification exception, such as completed_with_approved_verification_exception, and must never be represented as an automated test pass or full certification. Each testing capability family supports Auto, On, and Off: Auto discovers and selects or installs within authority; On is required and blocks or asks for authority when unavailable; Off prohibits use and installation for that capability without implying a pass. Approve And Build atomically writes the immutable pack, user approval receipt, and PlanApproved transactional-outbox event so approval cannot be committed without a recoverable downstream trigger. PlanApproved uses a deterministic idempotency key derived from project_id, pack_id, pack version, and pack hash; duplicate delivery returns the existing PlanCompileRun rather than creating another run. The runtime schema includes contract_mode, launch_policy, runtime_adapter, runtime_enablement_ref, and runtime_policy_snapshot_ref; the design_only branch preserves disabled bootstrap semantics, while the finished-product native_runtime branch defaults to automatic_after_approval through native_puppet_master_adapter with runtime enablement evidence. Each stage card defines exact inputs, outputs, algorithms, bounded units, read/write authority, required parallelism, validators, retry and repair routes, currentness behavior, terminal states, and evidence/receipt requirements. A certified WorkNodeRequest has non-empty objective, source PlanUnits and acceptance units, bounded read/write/implementation surfaces, typed dependencies, authority, model/capability routing, test binding, repository currentness, evidence requirements, idempotency, cancellation, and no unsupported or placeholder content. After Activation Decision accepts the graph, Executor materializes canonical WorkNodeRecord objects from accepted WorkNodeRequests and emits materialization receipts. WorkNodeRecord includes worknode_id, workgraph_id and revision, source_request_id, source PlanUnit and acceptance refs, objective, surfaces, typed readiness predicates, lifecycle, attempts and retries, authority, model, tests, repository/worktree/safe-point refs, evidence, currentness, cancellation, invalidation, and replan generation. Existing project_plan_node schema remains an import or compatibility contract with an explicit adapter and must not silently become the canonical runtime WorkNodeRecord. Work dispatch, change, test, retry, and completion receipts use worknode_id and attempt_id plus source_request_id and graph revision; a WorkNodeRequest reference alone is not sufficient runtime identity. The GoalRun activation and certification flow is retired by DL-478. Within the stable pm.plans_to_code_handoff.v1 schema document, plans-to-code runtime-capable v2 native_runtime records carry schema version, project, planning run, plan pack, PlanCompileRun, WorkGraph and revision, WorkNode, attempt, actor, status, revision, hashes, currentness, correlation, causation, idempotency, source, artifact, evidence, and supersession fields as applicable. Planning Wizard workflow and Auditor own AuditCycle, AuditFinding, RepairAttempt, AuditClosure, and CertificationReceipt records rather than Goal Runtime or superseded experimental workflow machinery. The final audit controller must launch multiple bounded read-only specialist agents in parallel for distinct defect families, persist assignments and results, reduce findings, run bounded repairs, and re-audit until all findings are durably closed or a true typed blocker remains. Audit findings have stable finding keys, source and artifact hashes, closure status, evidence, reason, repair attempts, and reopen conditions so unchanged closed findings become previously closed rather than recurring forever. The only permitted incomplete item is a user_approved_incomplete_item naming the exact artifact and span, reason, risk, approver, downstream disposition, expiration or reopen condition, and evidence; broad permission to leave TODOs is invalid. App Assistant Plans/Deep Plan are APR-073/074 and CV-368, separate from these Project-required PRD/PlanningRun/NamedPlan/Orchestrator records. Wizard handoff first establishes a real Project and fresh exact-version approval; no fields here become nullable to admit app work.

The schema draft records required artifact families without enabling PlanCompile.
The schema draft distinguishes the current bootstrap/v1 design_only branch from the PNC-015 runtime-capable v2 native_runtime branch.
The schema draft discriminates payload schemas by artifact_kind and defines every artifact_kind payload under $defs.
The row-by-row handoff matrix below maps every required transition to schema_payload, producer, consumer, evidence_refs, and PlanUnit refs.
PlanCompile consumes the Executor-owned execution_unit_context schema by reference and does not redefine context fields.
`cmd.plan_compile.open_build` is a route/open or post-build reveal command with projected availability, disabled reason, and explicit receipt; it must not fabricate a PlanCompile success event or claim runtime activation while the branch is design_only.
Codex bootstrap external GUI-agent request is documented as a bootstrap artifact only, not a built Puppet Master setting.
Plan_To_Node_Compilation owns the Plan Compile side of the Plans-to-Code Handoff Matrix. Every transition from Planning Wizard Approve And Build approval and the PlanApproved handoff into PlanCompileRun state, then through PlanCompile, Executor intake, source-control preflight, dispatch, tests, Auditor verification, repair, promotion, graph completion, and certification must name row_id, transition, source_artifact, destination_artifact, producer, consumer, owner, validator, receipt, schema_payload, retry_route, rollback_route, user_escalation_condition, evidence_refs, and plan_unit_refs. For the current bootstrap/v1 matrix, Plan Compile source authority is the immutable ApprovedPlanPack plus frozen PlanUnit and acceptance-unit indexes; the Planning Wizard ledger remains source and reasoning lineage rather than executable Plan Compile authority. The shared `Plans/plans_to_code_handoff.schema.json` document keeps top-level `schema_id` at `pm.plans_to_code_handoff.v1`; within that stable document identity, the current bootstrap/v1 branch is the historical design_only contract with launch disabled, while PNC-015 owns the runtime-capable v2 native_runtime branch with runtime enablement evidence. PlanCompile and handoff rows consume the Executor-owned `execution_unit_context` contract only by reference through `Plans/Executor_Protocol.md` and `Plans/execution_unit_context.schema.json`; they must not define a local field list, omit schema_version from persisted context payloads, or persist secrets in context payloads. The schema draft in Plans/plans_to_code_handoff.schema.json records handoff_matrix, handoff_row, PlanCompileRun, stage card, compile worklist, NodeSeed candidate, NodeSeed review, WorkGraph draft, WorkNode request, compiler model routing, Codex work package, Codex external GUI-agent request, PlanCompile receipt, automated testing reports, test cases, test run receipts, visual evidence, source-control receipts, WorkNode dispatch/change/completion receipts, Auditor cycle and verification receipts, repair attempt receipts, legacy validation_pass_report compatibility aliases, model resolution receipts, and ExecutorIntakeReport shapes for the disabled design_only branch plus the runtime-aware native_runtime branch; neither branch creates runtime artifacts by itself. The PlanApproved handoff records the approval_cas_receipt, transactional outbox requirement, and deterministic idempotency_key over project_id, pack identity/version/hash, PlanningRun revision, topic map version, PlanUnit and acceptance-unit index hashes, testing policy hash, project-context snapshot hash, and final audit/closure hash so approval cannot create duplicate or stale PlanCompileRun state. The handoff matrix names Plans to WorkNodes as a design-only bridge. Do not expose this bridge as a built Puppet Master setting. Its schema boundary is the single `Plans/plans_to_code_handoff.schema.json` draft, whose `$defs` include a concrete strict payload definition for every `artifact_kind` enum value and whose top-level discriminator maps each `artifact_kind` to the matching `payload` schema, including `handoff_matrix`, `handoff_row`, `plan_compile_run`, `node_seed_candidate`, `worknode_request`, `test_capability_report`, `source_control_receipt`, `source_control_preflight_receipt`, `worknode_dispatch_receipt`, `auditor_cycle_report` and `validation_pass_report` while preserving source_artifact, destination_artifact, retry_route, rollback_route, and user_escalation_condition fields. Within that single schema_id=v1 draft, current bootstrap/v1 records use the historical design_only branch and runtime-capable v2 records use native_runtime only with runtime enablement evidence. H-001 through H-017 must remain present exactly once, and each row's schema_payload refs must resolve to concrete `$defs` or artifact_kind payloads. The historical per-artifact filename tokens `plan_compile_run.schema.json`, `node_seed_candidate.schema.json`, `worknode_request.schema.json`, and `test_capability_report.schema.json` are compatibility aliases for `$defs` in `Plans/plans_to_code_handoff.schema.json`, not separate schema files. Approval creates an immutable, versioned Approved PRD Pack containing the primary PRD, accepted PRD-ledger snapshot, source manifest, traceability, assumptions and constraints, open questions, quality report, approval receipt, hashes, and version identity. Edits after approval create a new draft based on the approved version and require a new approval event; previous Approved PRD Packs remain immutable and addressable. Planning Wizard accepts an Approved PRD Pack, normalized imported requirements pack, or structured Assistant Chat handoff seed, preserving source identity, version, hashes, warnings, amendments, and lineage. PlanningRun owns source pack identity, project and work-intent context, thread group, global planning ledger, dynamic topic map, topic threads, topic plan drafts, amendments, invalidations, audit cycles, final plan pack, status, hashes, and handoff events. Planning Wizard child-thread identity uses thread_type planning_wizard plus thread_role values for intake, topic, final_integration, audit_review, and final_review, bound to Planning Run membership rather than minted as unrelated top-level thread families. The controller can add, split, merge, rename, defer, reopen, reorder, and mark topics impacted, recording the reason, source refs, dependencies, user-visible origin, and resulting invalidations. A later decision that changes a prior topic's assumptions or outputs marks affected topic drafts stale_due_to_dependency_change, stale_due_to_new_scope, or requires_recompile/requires_reaudit and propagates impact through typed topic dependencies. New information during planning becomes a planning clarification, immutable Planning Amendment, out_of_current_approved_scope item, or PRD revision request according to materiality and impact. Disabling or restricting automated testing requires a durable testing_policy_override explicitly approved by the user for exact projects, PlanUnits, WorkNodes, capability classes, reasons, risks, and reopen conditions. Affected work remains truthfully marked with an approved verification exception, such as completed_with_approved_verification_exception, and must never be represented as an automated test pass or full certification. Each testing capability family supports Auto, On, and Off: Auto discovers and selects or installs within authority; On is required and blocks or asks for authority when unavailable; Off prohibits use and installation for that capability without implying a pass. Approve And Build atomically writes the immutable pack, user approval receipt, and PlanApproved transactional-outbox event so approval cannot be committed without a recoverable downstream trigger. PlanApproved uses a deterministic idempotency key derived from project_id, pack_id, pack version, and pack hash; duplicate delivery returns the existing PlanCompileRun rather than creating another run. The runtime schema includes contract_mode, launch_policy, runtime_adapter, runtime_enablement_ref, and runtime_policy_snapshot_ref; the design_only branch preserves disabled bootstrap semantics, while the finished-product native_runtime branch defaults to automatic_after_approval through native_puppet_master_adapter with runtime enablement evidence. Each stage card defines exact inputs, outputs, algorithms, bounded units, read/write authority, required parallelism, validators, retry and repair routes, currentness behavior, terminal states, and evidence/receipt requirements. A certified WorkNodeRequest has non-empty objective, source PlanUnits and acceptance units, bounded read/write/implementation surfaces, typed dependencies, authority, model/capability routing, test binding, repository currentness, evidence requirements, idempotency, cancellation, and no unsupported or placeholder content. After Activation Decision accepts the graph, Executor materializes canonical WorkNodeRecord objects from accepted WorkNodeRequests and emits materialization receipts. WorkNodeRecord includes worknode_id, workgraph_id and revision, source_request_id, source PlanUnit and acceptance refs, objective, surfaces, typed readiness predicates, lifecycle, attempts and retries, authority, model, tests, repository/worktree/safe-point refs, evidence, currentness, cancellation, invalidation, and replan generation. Planning Wizard workflow and Auditor own AuditCycle, AuditFinding, RepairAttempt, AuditClosure, and CertificationReceipt records rather than Goal Runtime or superseded experimental workflow machinery. The final audit controller must launch multiple bounded read-only specialist agents in parallel for distinct defect families, persist assignments and results, reduce findings, run bounded repairs, and re-audit until all findings are durably closed or a true typed blocker remains. Audit findings have stable finding keys, source and artifact hashes, closure status, evidence, reason, repair attempts, and reopen conditions so unchanged closed findings become previously closed rather than recurring forever. The only permitted incomplete item is a user_approved_incomplete_item naming the exact artifact and span, reason, risk, approver, downstream disposition, expiration or reopen condition, and evidence; broad permission to leave TODOs is invalid. App Assistant Plans/Deep Plan are APR-073/074 and CV-368, separate from these Project-required PRD/PlanningRun/NamedPlan/Orchestrator records. The Approved Plan Pack carries a hash-addressed project-context snapshot containing repository identity, host, path, branch, remotes, dirty state, codebase scan facts, test-capability facts, and currentness conditions, and the approval_cas_receipt binds that snapshot to the exact PlanningRun revision, topic map version, pack hash, PlanUnit index hash, acceptance-unit index hash, testing policy hash, and final audit/closure hash shown at final review. Plan Compile and Executor provisioning must compare live repository and environment state against the approved snapshot and route stale facts through bounded re-analysis or recompile rather than executing against invalid assumptions. Keep the current plans-to-code handoff v1 schema_id as the stable shared schema document for the historical design-only contract with launch disabled, and introduce the versioned runtime-capable v2 identity as the native_runtime branch inside that document rather than silently changing v1 branch semantics. The runtime schema includes contract_mode, launch_policy, runtime_adapter, runtime_enablement_ref, and runtime_policy_snapshot_ref; the design_only branch preserves const-false launch gates, while the finished-product native_runtime branch defaults to automatic_after_approval through native_puppet_master_adapter and requires runtime enablement evidence. PlanCompileRun persists stage, cursor, bounded worklists, assignment receipts, source hashes, currentness status, blockers, repairs, artifacts, retries, cancellation, supersession, and exact next action across context and process restarts. Changes after approval create successor ApprovedPlanPack versions; during compilation or execution a PlanDiffImpactReport classifies unaffected, already safe, needs recompile, and invalidated lanes and only continues unaffected work when dependencies and write surfaces prove safety. The PlanUnit index/readiness Goal regenerates only allowed Plans/.plan_index outputs, reports exact blockers, and creates no WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, candidates, executable queues, implementation files, or production tasks.

No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, GoalRuns, implementation files, generated governance artifacts, or production build tasks are created by this compile.
Approval creates an immutable, versioned Approved PRD Pack containing the primary PRD, accepted PRD-ledger snapshot, source manifest, traceability, assumptions and constraints, open questions, quality report, approval receipt, hashes, and version identity. Edits after approval create a new draft based on the approved version and require a new approval event; previous Approved PRD Packs remain immutable and addressable. Planning Wizard accepts an Approved PRD Pack, normalized imported requirements pack, or structured Assistant Chat handoff seed, preserving source identity, version, hashes, warnings, amendments, and lineage. PlanningRun owns source pack identity, project and work-intent context, thread group, global planning ledger, dynamic topic map, topic threads, topic plan drafts, amendments, invalidations, audit cycles, final plan pack, status, hashes, and handoff events. Planning Wizard child-thread identity uses thread_type planning_wizard plus thread_role values for intake, topic, final_integration, audit_review, and final_review, bound to Planning Run membership rather than minted as unrelated top-level thread families. The controller can add, split, merge, rename, defer, reopen, reorder, and mark topics impacted, recording the reason, source refs, dependencies, user-visible origin, and resulting invalidations. A later decision that changes a prior topic's assumptions or outputs marks affected topic drafts stale_due_to_dependency_change, stale_due_to_new_scope, or requires_recompile/requires_reaudit and propagates impact through typed topic dependencies. New information during planning becomes a planning clarification, immutable Planning Amendment, out_of_current_approved_scope item, or PRD revision request according to materiality and impact. Disabling or restricting automated testing requires a durable testing_policy_override explicitly approved by the user for exact projects, PlanUnits, WorkNodes, capability classes, reasons, risks, and reopen conditions. Affected work remains truthfully marked with an approved verification exception, such as completed_with_approved_verification_exception, and must never be represented as an automated test pass or full certification. Each testing capability family supports Auto, On, and Off: Auto discovers and selects or installs within authority; On is required and blocks or asks for authority when unavailable; Off prohibits use and installation for that capability without implying a pass. Approve And Build atomically writes the immutable pack, user approval receipt, and PlanApproved transactional-outbox event so approval cannot be committed without a recoverable downstream trigger. PlanApproved uses a deterministic idempotency key derived from project_id, pack_id, pack version, and pack hash; duplicate delivery returns the existing PlanCompileRun rather than creating another run. The runtime schema includes contract_mode, launch_policy, runtime_adapter, runtime_enablement_ref, and runtime_policy_snapshot_ref; the design_only branch preserves disabled bootstrap semantics, while the finished-product native_runtime branch defaults to automatic_after_approval through native_puppet_master_adapter with runtime enablement evidence. Each stage card defines exact inputs, outputs, algorithms, bounded units, read/write authority, required parallelism, validators, retry and repair routes, currentness behavior, terminal states, and evidence/receipt requirements. A certified WorkNodeRequest has non-empty objective, source PlanUnits and acceptance units, bounded read/write/implementation surfaces, typed dependencies, authority, model/capability routing, test binding, repository currentness, evidence requirements, idempotency, cancellation, and no unsupported or placeholder content. After Activation Decision accepts the graph, Executor materializes canonical WorkNodeRecord objects from accepted WorkNodeRequests and emits materialization receipts. WorkNodeRecord includes worknode_id, workgraph_id and revision, source_request_id, source PlanUnit and acceptance refs, objective, surfaces, typed readiness predicates, lifecycle, attempts and retries, authority, model, tests, repository/worktree/safe-point refs, evidence, currentness, cancellation, invalidation, and replan generation. Existing project_plan_node schema remains an import or compatibility contract with an explicit adapter and must not silently become the canonical runtime WorkNodeRecord. Work dispatch, change, test, retry, and completion receipts use worknode_id and attempt_id plus source_request_id and graph revision; a WorkNodeRequest reference alone is not sufficient runtime identity. The GoalRun activation and certification flow is retired by DL-478. Within the stable pm.plans_to_code_handoff.v1 schema document, plans-to-code runtime-capable v2 native_runtime records carry schema version, project, planning run, plan pack, PlanCompileRun, WorkGraph and revision, WorkNode, attempt, actor, status, revision, hashes, currentness, correlation, causation, idempotency, source, artifact, evidence, and supersession fields as applicable. Planning Wizard workflow and Auditor own AuditCycle, AuditFinding, RepairAttempt, AuditClosure, and CertificationReceipt records rather than Goal Runtime or superseded experimental workflow machinery. The final audit controller must launch multiple bounded read-only specialist agents in parallel for distinct defect families, persist assignments and results, reduce findings, run bounded repairs, and re-audit until all findings are durably closed or a true typed blocker remains. Audit findings have stable finding keys, source and artifact hashes, closure status, evidence, reason, repair attempts, and reopen conditions so unchanged closed findings become previously closed rather than recurring forever. The only permitted incomplete item is a user_approved_incomplete_item naming the exact artifact and span, reason, risk, approver, downstream disposition, expiration or reopen condition, and evidence; broad permission to leave TODOs is invalid. App Assistant Plans/Deep Plan are APR-073/074 and CV-368, separate from these Project-required PRD/PlanningRun/NamedPlan/Orchestrator records. Wizard handoff first establishes a real Project and fresh exact-version approval; no fields here become nullable to admit app work.

dependency_anchors.text:
Every Executor handoff has artifact, owner, validator, receipt, retry, rollback, and escalation fields.
WorkNode execution receipts distinguish dispatch, preflight, safe point, change, test, audit, repair, promotion, and completion.
Code completion is certified from receipts, tests, source-control state, Auditor result, blockers, and final evidence, not worker prose.
A run with unresolved validator failure, verifier unavailability, or exhausted repair budget cannot be certified complete.
An exhausted repair budget stops the run blocked with budget_exhausted; ask_exception adds only an owner exception request through the DL-081 route, never a degraded or clean finish.
Executor contributes the execution side of the Plans-to-Code Handoff Matrix. A complete WorkNode execution flow emits worknode_dispatch_receipt, source_control_preflight_receipt, safe_point_receipt, worknode_change_receipt, test_run_receipt, auditor_verification_receipt, repair_attempt_receipt when needed, merge_or_promotion_receipt when applicable, worknode_completion_receipt, and finalization evidence. Each transition records source artifact, destination artifact, owner, validator, receipt, retry route, rollback route, and user escalation condition. Worker claims are never enough to certify code complete. The receipt chain preserves source_artifact, destination_artifact, retry_route, rollback_route, all WorkNodes terminal, all automated tests passed or dispositioned, and artifact-backed handoff evidence before code completion is certified. The source-control chain must preserve the same repo_id, worktree_id, worktree_path, branch_ref, branch_head_state, baseline_commit_oid, head_commit_oid, safe_point_id, changed_files, conflict_refs, rollback_available, rollback_ref, and restore_command_or_action through preflight, safe point creation, mutation/change, optional promotion, finalization, and completion certification. A run is certified complete only after every required verification, receipt, authority, and finalization gate clears. Unresolved validator failure, verifier unavailability, or an exhausted repair budget never yields certified complete; existing owner policy determines the disposition of the first two. An exhausted repair budget stops the run blocked with BlockedReasonCode budget_exhausted. When Settings planning.verification.repair-budget-exhaustion is ask_exception, that blocked stop also asks the project owner, through the DL-081 approved verification exception route, whether to finish as completed_with_approved_verification_exception, with the approver and the remaining risks recorded; the run is never shown as a clean pass. Until that route is bound (GRS-065 keeps it separately unbound), the run stays blocked. There is no degraded run state.

The live owner doc preserves every source atom listed in source_atom_ids without treating the ledger as canonical product prose.
Exact tokens, negative constraints, owner hints, and accepted corrections remain available to future audits through this PlanUnit.
No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, GoalRuns, implementation files, generated governance artifacts, or production build tasks are created by this compile.
Approve And Build records an approval CAS receipt and fails closed when final-review currentness inputs drift.
The PlanCompileRun identity is created or returned synchronously; projection identity reconciliation cannot be the source of run identity truth.
`cmd.runtime.approve` consumes canonical approval/currentness inputs, records UICommandResponse and approval/dispatch receipt refs, and emits only canonical runtime events or explicit receipts, never `runtime.command_applied`.
Approve And Build first validates a compare-and-swap approval boundary over the PlanningRun revision, topic map version, immutable pack identity, pack version, pack hash, project-context snapshot hash, PlanUnit index hash, acceptance-unit index hash, testing policy hash, and final audit/closure hash shown in final review. It then atomically writes the immutable pack, approval_cas_receipt, user approval receipt, and PlanApproved transactional-outbox event so approval cannot be committed without a recoverable downstream trigger. PlanApproved uses a deterministic idempotency key derived from project_id, pack_id, pack version, pack hash, and approval CAS inputs; duplicate delivery returns the existing PlanCompileRun rather than creating another run. In the finished-product native runtime contract, ordinary Approve And Build flow immediately creates or resumes exactly one PlanCompileRun and returns its identity synchronously before projection reconciliation; optional HITL checkpoints are policy exceptions, not the default. During the current bootstrap ledger-to-Plans lane, this remains product-runtime canon and does not launch PlanCompile. For broad stages the controller computes a bounded worklist and mandatory minimum parallel assignments, launches read-only subagents, records assignment and completion receipts, and rejects certification when required parallel work is absent. A required broad stage may reduce scope or block with a typed runtime-capability error, but it may not silently substitute one broad agent for mandatory parallel analysis or review. Activation requires all required active-scope WorkNodeRequests to be accepted together; optional work must be explicitly excluded or deferred before activation, and a mixed result cannot silently start a partial build. Orchestrator may show launch and provisioning progress before activation, but it marks the build running and exposes runnable WorkNodes only after the atomic activation commit and durable start receipt. Activation persists activation_pending, records_materialized, entrypoints_queued, start_event_pending, active, and cancelled_before_mutation states; retries resume idempotently, duplicate commands return the existing PlanCompileRun, and cancellation routes according to whether mutation began. Planning Wizard workflow and Auditor own AuditCycle, AuditFinding, RepairAttempt, AuditClosure, and CertificationReceipt records rather than Goal Runtime (DL-472, DL-478). The final audit controller must launch multiple bounded read-only specialist agents in parallel for distinct defect families, persist assignments and results, reduce findings, run bounded repairs, and re-audit until all findings are durably closed or a true typed blocker remains. Audit and repair subagents inspect, classify, compare, and propose; the Planning Run controller or assigned canonical artifact owner performs serialized writes, updates closures, and issues certification. Classify gaps as auto_resolvable, safe_default_with_assumption, defer_to_plan_compile, defer_to_worknode_system, requires_user_policy_decision, requires_user_risk_acceptance, requires_external_credential, or true infrastructure/runtime blocker.

The handoff schema carries the runtime-v2 PlanCompileRun fields `contract_mode`, `launch_policy`, `runtime_adapter`, `runtime_enablement_ref`, and `runtime_policy_snapshot_ref`; design_only records remain disabled, while native_runtime records require enablement evidence before automatic launch.
No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, GoalRuns, implementation files, generated governance artifacts, or production build tasks are created by this compile.
Approval creates an immutable, versioned Approved PRD Pack containing the primary PRD, accepted PRD-ledger snapshot, source manifest, traceability, assumptions and constraints, open questions, quality report, approval receipt, hashes, and version identity. Edits after approval create a new draft based on the approved version and require a new approval event; previous Approved PRD Packs remain immutable and addressable. Planning Wizard accepts an Approved PRD Pack, normalized imported requirements pack, or structured Assistant Chat handoff seed, preserving source identity, version, hashes, warnings, amendments, and lineage. PlanningRun owns source pack identity, project and work-intent context, thread group, global planning ledger, dynamic topic map, topic threads, topic plan drafts, amendments, invalidations, audit cycles, final plan pack, status, hashes, and handoff events. Planning Wizard child-thread identity uses thread_type planning_wizard plus thread_role values for intake, topic, final_integration, audit_review, and final_review, bound to Planning Run membership rather than minted as unrelated top-level thread families. The controller can add, split, merge, rename, defer, reopen, reorder, and mark topics impacted, recording the reason, source refs, dependencies, user-visible origin, and resulting invalidations. A later decision that changes a prior topic's assumptions or outputs marks affected topic drafts stale_due_to_dependency_change, stale_due_to_new_scope, or requires_recompile/requires_reaudit and propagates impact through typed topic dependencies. New information during planning becomes a planning clarification, immutable Planning Amendment, out_of_current_approved_scope item, or PRD revision request according to materiality and impact. Disabling or restricting automated testing requires a durable testing_policy_override explicitly approved by the user for exact projects, PlanUnits, WorkNodes, capability classes, reasons, risks, and reopen conditions. Affected work remains truthfully marked with an approved verification exception, such as completed_with_approved_verification_exception, and must never be represented as an automated test pass or full certification. Each testing capability family supports Auto, On, and Off: Auto discovers and selects or installs within authority; On is required and blocks or asks for authority when unavailable; Off prohibits use and installation for that capability without implying a pass. Approve And Build atomically writes the immutable pack, user approval receipt, and PlanApproved transactional-outbox event so approval cannot be committed without a recoverable downstream trigger. PlanApproved uses a deterministic idempotency key derived from project_id, pack_id, pack version, and pack hash; duplicate delivery returns the existing PlanCompileRun rather than creating another run. The runtime schema includes contract_mode, launch_policy, runtime_adapter, runtime_enablement_ref, and runtime_policy_snapshot_ref; the design_only branch preserves disabled bootstrap semantics, while the finished-product native_runtime branch defaults to automatic_after_approval through native_puppet_master_adapter with runtime enablement evidence. Each stage card defines exact inputs, outputs, algorithms, bounded units, read/write authority, required parallelism, validators, retry and repair routes, currentness behavior, terminal states, and evidence/receipt requirements. A certified WorkNodeRequest has non-empty objective, source PlanUnits and acceptance units, bounded read/write/implementation surfaces, typed dependencies, authority, model/capability routing, test binding, repository currentness, evidence requirements, idempotency, cancellation, and no unsupported or placeholder content. After Activation Decision accepts the graph, Executor materializes canonical WorkNodeRecord objects from accepted WorkNodeRequests and emits materialization receipts. WorkNodeRecord includes worknode_id, workgraph_id and revision, source_request_id, source PlanUnit and acceptance refs, objective, surfaces, typed readiness predicates, lifecycle, attempts and retries, authority, model, tests, repository/worktree/safe-point refs, evidence, currentness, cancellation, invalidation, and replan generation. Existing project_plan_node schema remains an import or compatibility contract with an explicit adapter and must not silently become the canonical runtime WorkNodeRecord. Work dispatch, change, test, retry, and completion receipts use worknode_id and attempt_id plus source_request_id and graph revision; a WorkNodeRequest reference alone is not sufficient runtime identity. The GoalRun activation and certification flow is retired by DL-478. Within the stable pm.plans_to_code_handoff.v1 schema document, plans-to-code runtime-capable v2 native_runtime records carry schema version, project, planning run, plan pack, PlanCompileRun, WorkGraph and revision, WorkNode, attempt, actor, status, revision, hashes, currentness, correlation, causation, idempotency, source, artifact, evidence, and supersession fields as applicable. Planning Wizard workflow and Auditor own AuditCycle, AuditFinding, RepairAttempt, AuditClosure, and CertificationReceipt records rather than Goal Runtime or superseded experimental workflow machinery. The final audit controller must launch multiple bounded read-only specialist agents in parallel for distinct defect families, persist assignments and results, reduce findings, run bounded repairs, and re-audit until all findings are durably closed or a true typed blocker remains. Audit findings have stable finding keys, source and artifact hashes, closure status, evidence, reason, repair attempts, and reopen conditions so unchanged closed findings become previously closed rather than recurring forever. The only permitted incomplete item is a user_approved_incomplete_item naming the exact artifact and span, reason, risk, approver, downstream disposition, expiration or reopen condition, and evidence; broad permission to leave TODOs is invalid. App Assistant Plans/Deep Plan are APR-073/074 and CV-368, separate from these Project-required PRD/PlanningRun/NamedPlan/Orchestrator records. Wizard handoff first establishes a real Project and fresh exact-version approval; no fields here become nullable to admit app work.

**This is a PLAN DOCUMENT ONLY** -- No code changes have been made. This document contains:

- Historical intent-based workflow definitions retained for source-lineage compatibility.
- Historical GUI and flow examples that current PRD Builder, Planning Wizard, Final GUI, GitHub, and source-control owner docs may consume after revalidation.

As of 2026-06-21 this document is not an active canonical owner for current PRD/Planning product behavior, requirements flow, GUI, command, runtime, PlanCompile, Executor, or Orchestrator implementation. This table is an ownership router, not a peer product owner. Later accepted owner text below supersedes the conflicting live behavior while older text remains source-lineage only.

Planning Wizard owns wizard_status, the wizard's own lifecycle enum: setup (wizard instance and project setup are being prepared), requirements (requirements upload, PRD Builder, or canonical requirements merge is active), interview (adaptive interview phase is active), validating (Contract Unification and the Auditor validation loop are running), attention_required (the current clarification or review loop can still resolve the issue set), blocked (automatic progress cannot continue without new input, recovery, or replan), ready_to_execute (validated package is ready to launch execution), complete (wizard finished successfully), and cancelled (user cancelled). Builder bundle state, agent activity run state, and executor node status are separate state families and are not conflated with wizard_status. attention_required means the current clarification cycle can continue and answering the current questions may unblock progress; blocked means clarification rounds are exhausted or progress otherwise cannot continue automatically. A Debug investigation budget trip may surface as failed or attention_required depending on whether user recovery is meaningful, but its stop_reason_code stays investigation.budget_exhausted and carries budget_kind. When the requirements-quality check of Decision_Policy §6.4 ends with non-empty needs_user_clarification[], the wizard becomes attention_required: Proceed and Start Run are disabled and the step that triggered the issue shows a lock icon or warning badge. It returns to its normal state only when every needs_user_clarification[] entry is answered and the re-run with those answers injected produces verdict PASS with an empty needs_user_clarification[]. The wizard stays attention_required while the current clarification or review loop can still resolve the issue set, and escalates to blocked when clarification_round_count reaches the Decision_Policy §6.5 cap (DP-064, 3 cycles) without clearing the blocking issues, or when the next required action can no longer be completed inside the current flow (for example auth recovery, explicit user correction outside the inline form, or replan approval). The wizard UX distinguishes clarification still pending (attention_required), blocked on user correction, auth, approval, or integrity (blocked), and degraded but still usable draft structure before graph lock. In blocked, Proceed and Start Run stay disabled, the UI copy explains that repeated clarification attempts did not resolve the issue set, the latest canonical quality report is preserved, and requirements are not rewritten automatically without new explicit user input. Blocked persistence uses wizard_status = blocked with blocked_reason_code. A wizard blocked record persists wizard_id, wizard_step, blocked_reason_code, clarification_round_count, report_ref, resume_url?, decomposition_degraded, degradation_reason?, replan_generation?, and attempted_recovery_action_ids[]; wizard state also carries attention_required_reason and attention_required_report_path, the latest blocking requirements quality report. The legacy blocked field names is_blocked, blocked_info, blocked_state, and blocked_episode_ref are non-canonical aliases and are not introduced in new wizard state. A wizard leaves blocked only when materially new user input creates a new issue set, the external prerequisite named by blocked_reason_code is actually resolved, a new replan_generation begins for the wizard context, or the wizard is cancelled; reopening the same blocked wizard without one of those changes does not clear blocked and does not reset clarification_round_count. Wizard packets support both wizard_attention_required and wizard_blocked with the shared fields wizard_id, wizard_step, report_ref, resume_url, thread_id?, and status, so Dashboard, thread, and resume deep-link behavior works for both states.

### 6.5 Clarification-round limits (Planning Wizard)

Decision Policy owns the clarification-round limits; they apply to the Planning Wizard's clarification cycles (DL-330, Jared 2026-11-05). They moved here from retired `Plans/chain-wizard-flexibility.md §15.5` unchanged.

A clarification cycle is one complete sequence of:
1. a `requirements_quality_report` with non-empty `needs_user_clarification[]`,
2. user answer submission,
3. automatic re-run of the requirements-quality Auditor loop of §6.4 with the answers injected.

Limits:
- One Planning Wizard instance allows at most 3 clarification cycles, counted in `clarification_round_count`.
- Cycles 1-2: the wizard stays in the active clarification path (`attention_required`) while follow-up questions remain.
- When cycle 3 still produces non-empty `needs_user_clarification[]`, the Planning Wizard moves to `blocked` as `Plans/Planning_Wizard.md` (PWIZ-038) defines; that unit owns the blocked state, its record and its clear rule, and reopening the same blocked wizard does not reset `clarification_round_count`.
- After the cap, Puppet Master MUST preserve the latest canonical quality report and MUST NOT auto-rewrite requirements further without new explicit user input.
- User override: the UI MUST offer an explicit override to continue with a manual user decision only when the user acknowledges the remaining risk and the downstream gate permits override for that category. That override MUST be recorded as evidence.

### PWIZ-027 - Research Decision Dispositions Into Topics And Amendments

```yaml
plan_unit_id: PWIZ-027
unit_type: requirement
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Planning_Wizard.md
canonical_text: 'Research/audit decision packets are reviewed in the existing embedded Assistant Chat during PlanningRun
  topic, audit and amendment work. Planning Wizard consumes recorded exact-item dispositions: approval permits feature
  planning only, denial excludes the proposal, denial with changes preserves the exact requested change for existing
  amendment processing without approving the changed proposal, and questions keep the same item pending until a
  user disposition. The final Approve And Build authority remains separate.'
gui_related: true
gui_classification_reason: Defines the visible planning handoff and decision-card presentation or its user approval
  boundary.
split_recommended: false
depends_on:
- PWIZ-003
- PWIZ-005
- PWIZ-010
- PWIZ-014
- ACD-459
- CV-328
- SP-258
unblocks: []
acceptance_criteria:
- The full artifact contains every review item and remains openable through cmd.nav.open_subject before, during
  and after individual card responses; opening it neither advances the review nor changes a disposition.
- Topic research, audit findings and amendments route product choices through the Chat-owned one-at-a-time decision
  profile with exact typed packet/item/revision and source lineage. Existing general questionnaires remain multi-question
  and are not forced into this sequencing.
- Approve adds the reviewed feature to authorized topic planning; Deny excludes it from accepted scope while preserving

  Settled items are not asked again, and missing/unavailable readback cannot be represented as an empty undecided
  packet or a successful disposition.

  integration under existing readiness and currentness gates. Feature Approve does not invoke Approve And Build,

  the final reviewed plan through that existing path.

- Plans/ledgers/v2/pldg-20260909-001-research-decision-review/source_shards/decision_authority_20260909.md

- Deny with changes
- Ask a question

- No agent answers on the user’s behalf, dismissal auto-submit, automatic approval/denial or mutation of an immutable
```

An exact approved Plan/grant admits listed repo/registry/CI/deployment operations without repeated human clicks.
Grant-created exact object cleanup succeeds; pre-existing, same-name replacement, unrelated namespace/registry/repo, unlisted child kind and broad prune refuse.
Plan/account/target/permission/Stop/revocation drift prevents effect and cannot be repaired by an agent widening authority.
Children cannot mint grants or exceed parent/resource subsets; app Goal/Crew/Plan/schedule and cross-project messages cannot adopt a Project grant.
Unknown create/push is reconciled before retry; action projection includes actual target/authority and no unsafe invented Undo.
Build location scope follows the current person-allowed Project set, including later human additions, while each attempt freezes exactly one current selection.
YOLO/Auto/agents cannot add a Computer/device identity or widen operation/account/resource authority; historical exact grants are not upgraded implicitly.
O1–O3 approve a build grant once at exact human Plan approval for a Project-bound Planning Wizard/Orchestrator build. The review lists the repositories to create/push, registry namespaces/package/image/template destinations, CI configuration/execution and deployment targets with allowed operations. It also lists exclusions, risky cleanup eligibility and actions with no safe Undo. Approval of a Plan alone is not an unbounded grant: the person must approve the exact manifest. The Orchestrator then runs yolo within that grant without repeating ordinary per-action human clicks. Application chat Goals/Crew/Assistant Plan builds and schedules cannot issue a Project Orchestrator grant or obtain one through a message.

A BuildGrant binds grant_id and revision, actual issuing person and auth context/time, project_id, named_plan_id plus exact approved revision/hash, reserved build_run_id and the Project allowed-Computers policy reference, plus the exact approved Environment/route/account and operation/resource authority, allowed operation classes and typed stable target/resource selectors, permission snapshot and policy generation, validity/expiry when set, revocation generation and current user Stop epoch. A new-resource selector names exact provider/instance/account/parent container/namespace/name and creation constraints; it is not a wildcard for all future resources. A named existing resource binds immutable ID and only its listed permissible operations. Namespace grants enumerate allowed child kinds and operations; membership or a name prefix grants nothing. The permission snapshot and grant digest must be committed before build admission. Plan, target, account, permission ceiling or grant drift cannot widen authority; invalidated evidence blocks for refresh/review and any expansion requires another human decision.

Permissions is the sole grant writer. Canonical commands are cmd.build_grant.preview, cmd.build_grant.approve and cmd.build_grant.revoke with sole planned handlers handlers::permissions::build_grant_preview, handlers::permissions::build_grant_approve and handlers::permissions::build_grant_revoke. Preview is read-only and returns exact manifest/ref/hash/owner revisions, exclusions and blockers. Approve binds that current preview, current approved Plan/hash/build identity, expected grant-absence/revision CAS, issuer and idempotency key; it is human-only, including expansion. Revoke targets grant_id/revision under current actor authority, records revocation and fences all future child/provider dispatch. Existing run-owner Start/Stop/abort commands remain the execution controls; no second build runner or stop engine is introduced. Agent requests may prepare a preview but cannot resolve their own protected approval, issue, expand, renew or un-revoke the grant.

Each actual successful create appends a CreatedResourceManifest entry joined to the exact grant/build/task/operation receipt: provider/instance/account/parent, stable immutable resource ID/UID and generation, creation time, idempotency identity and verified result evidence. A failed or unknown create is not ownership proof; reconcile before adoption/retry. Pre-existing resources and a same-named replacement remain unowned regardless of selector or prefix. Observe identity/generation immediately before mutation/cleanup; replacement, owner drift, unknown provenance, user modification or other references/holds refuse the claimed automatic cleanup.

The grant can change its exact listed resources and delete only what the build itself demonstrably created. The retained Y1 risky actions—prune, remote branch/repository delete, destructive discard and Kubernetes delete/exec—avoid another ask only when that exact operation and verified grant-created object are inside the approved grant. A named pre-existing target may receive listed non-destructive build/deploy operations, but it never receives that risky-action exception. Broad Docker/system/registry prune cannot become a closed owned-resource cleanup by naming a namespace. There is no failure-setup or conversion-Undo automatic remote-repository deletion, no unrelated Project/environment mutation, no main/default/protected force-push, no secret value exposure or Recovery Kit export, no protected sign-in/trust/claim/Always bypass, no paid signup or human-only Azure team-project administration. Existing credentials may be consumed only as already-admitted opaque references under their owner; the grant never acquires or exports secret bytes.

Every coordinator, task/child admission and final local/remote effect checks exact grant/Plan/build/task/target/permission/ownership generations, parent ceiling and Stop/revocation epoch. Children receive at most their exact subset and cannot transfer authority to another Project/run/chat or broaden selectors. Logical operation idempotency binds exact operation/target/request under the grant; original historical receipts remain fixed and cannot re-authorize an attempt after drift. A remote indeterminate outcome reconciles before repeating work. Stop/revoke races fence new effects and late completions remain truthful rather than erased or re-executed.

O3's live What the build did list is an existing ObservableWork/History projection of every remote action and target, authority, outcome, time and linked owner receipt. It also exposes pending/blocked/unknown effects, Stop and available true Undo or explicitly labelled compensation/No safe Undo. It is not a new parallel action log or inferred build.* event family. Undo itself requires exact currentness/ownership/permission; revoking or stopping does not delete resources or reverse completed external actions. End-of-run YOLO scans/reconciliation and required verification still run. Static grant schemas/fixtures do not certify a native build, provider path or resource-ownership proof.

The Project Home Server Permissions owner holds the canonical grant, ownership manifest and authority-receipt references in the Project Vault under Storage-registered versioned families. These records are not disposable projections and must be included coherently in Project Backup and retained with build/audit/recovery holds. A restored grant is historical until the current owner, Plan, permission generation and Stop/revocation checks re-admit it; backup restore never resurrects an active grant by itself.

SP-353 is the sole physical owner for build_grant, created_resource_manifest and grant_revocation, referring to selected Permissions bodies and actual original authority sources. Missing immutable grant_revocation record/source materialization keeps that dispatch path unavailable; command request/result shapes or restored stale grants cannot substitute for current revocation authority. These records and required receipt/source refs retain independent audit/backup/hold lifetimes after chat conversion or Undo expiry.

DL-473 changes build location scope to any Computer currently allowed for this Project by a person, including one the person allows later: allowing that Computer is itself the person's act, so the build grant does not freeze an enumerated machine list at approval. Preview names this dynamic Project allowed-set policy and the then-current members plainly. Auto and agents cannot add Computers or device identities, widen that set or manufacture authority. A new Computer/device identity still asks even in YOLO. Allowing a Computer is only location authorization; new accounts, routes, environments, resources or operations outside existing authority retain their own protected approval and readiness checks. Removing/draining/revoking a Computer removes future eligibility and requires truthful active-work disposition; it never broadens another candidate.

Each dispatch freezes one exact Computer/Host/Environment/source/account/route/attempt/owner epoch and the current allowed-set generation, with fresh Plan/build/grant/permission/Stop/revocation rechecks under PS-148 and SIR-056. Other tasks may select another allowed Computer without new location approval; a started task moves only after safe checkpoint, reconciliation and old-owner fencing. The approved Project source/context must still verify on that actual Computer; dynamic location scope never approves a new baseline or target. Historical exact-location grants keep their historical meaning. A governed grant/context successor and per-dispatch selection receipt must carry this policy before native use; do not reinterpret a v1 record or hand-widen its closed schema.

def extract_plan_units() -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    units: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    errors: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    docs: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    for path in top_level_plan_docs():
        doc = cached_plan_doc(path)
        doc_units: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for match in PLAN_UNIT_FENCE_PATTERN.finditer(doc.text):
            block = match.group(1)
            if "plan_unit_id:" not in block:
                continue
            line_no = doc.line_no_for_offset(match.start())
            try:
                data = yaml.load(block, Loader=UniqueKeySafeLoader)
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - validator reports exact source.
                errors.append({"path": rel(path), "line": line_no, "error": "plan_unit_yaml_parse_error", "detail": str(exc)})
                continue
            if not isinstance(data, dict) or not data.get("plan_unit_id"):
                errors.append({"path": rel(path), "line": line_no, "error": "plan_unit_block_not_mapping"})
                continue
            unit = normalize_unit(
                data,
                path,
                line_no,
                doc.headings,
                adjacent_heading_before_line(doc.lines, line_no),
                source_doc_sha256=doc.sha256,
            )
            doc_units.append(unit)
            units.append(unit)

        docs.append(
            {
                "path": rel(path),
                "title": doc_title(path, doc.headings),
                "sha256": doc.sha256,
                "line_count": len(doc.lines),
                "heading_count": len(doc.headings),
                "plan_unit_ids": [str(unit.get("plan_unit_id", "")) for unit in doc_units],
            }
        )
    return units, errors, docs

## FABLE Deferred Action Concrete Repair Addendum - 2026-07-08

This addendum repairs non-runtime formatter rows without creating WorkNodes, implementation files, runtime artifacts, or PNC-019 evidence.

- Repairs `sfk-52b912e858e3f723a8838777`: formatter registration order is deterministic: built-in formatters in documented order, then project formatters sorted by `formatter_id`, then user/global formatters sorted by `formatter_id`. Ties are invalid and must fail validation with `duplicate_formatter_id`.


### FS-075 - Event Authority format.applied 1.0.0 — newly authored owner contract under DL-045.

```yaml
plan_unit_id: FS-075
unit_type: event_contract
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Formatters_System.md
canonical_text: |-
  format.applied 1.0.0 — newly authored owner contract under DL-045.
  Prepared without admission. Exact payload is Plans/event_payloads/format_applied.schema.json (pm.event_payload.format_applied.v1); no sibling or legacy spelling is admitted. Scope is project_only; project_id is a real immutable Project ID; application scope, null, empty and sentinel Project identities are forbidden. Payload project_id equals the envelope join. Existing CV-365 scope rules remain mandatory. Optional envelope lineage comes from the original operation, never ambient focus. Schema-only validity is insufficient.
  Producer: HTE formatter completion adapter. After a successful HTE write/edit formatter changes the tool output beyond whitespace, capture the tool-output and formatted-output evidence refs before publication. DAE remains unenforceable; whitespace-only changes and failed formatter output emit no format.applied.
  Freeze operation_id from fresh entropy in the original owning operation before its effect; preserve it and all source facts on retry/restart. Freeze the completion payload after owner success, before append. If the original operation cannot durably retain its intent/result, publication fails closed: never rerun the effect to reconstruct evidence. This contract creates no independent operation journal or stored value. The owner retains its existing intent/result and source refs under its existing storage contract.
  Adopt SP-286 first-AppendReceipt custody and CV-339 full-value v2 successor by name, including SP-336/SP-347 current group-commit rules. Validate admission before append; absent membership, unresolved retention or unavailable source custody prevents activation. Referenced bodies commit under SP-337 before append. The first original AppendReceipt is exposed only after the durable group frame; terminal event success publication follows that receipt. Lost acknowledgement returns that original full stored result and receipt, never a second effect or new receipt; equal identity with different semantic digest is a conflict, not a retry.
  Identity digest is SHA-256 of UTF-8 compact JSON array ["format.applied", "1.0.0", storage_instance_id, payload.project_id, payload.operation_id], with ensure_ascii=false, no whitespace and array order preserved. event_id="evt_"+digest; idempotency_key="format.applied:"+digest; family_revision=1.0.0, replay_policy=dedupe_by_idempotency_key, redaction_profile=secret_refs_only. Use Contracts_V0.md#EventRecord for the closed envelope, not a local field list. Envelope occurred_at_utc equals payload.timestamp byte-for-byte from the original HTE write/edit operation; retry time is forbidden. Storage alone assigns sequence_id, observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc. Full producer semantic digest uses EventRecord and CV-339, not only the identity tuple.
  Exact envelope joins for format.applied: actor_ref is the non-empty non-secret actor reference retained by the original HTE write/edit operation from its accepted owner request, never the retrying Client. correlation_id is the non-empty correlation_id frozen by that same original owner operation; payload.operation_id equals its immutable operation_id. Every handoff names artifact, owner, validator, receipt, retry, rollback, and escalation route.
```
The schema draft records required artifact families without enabling PlanCompile.
The schema draft distinguishes the current bootstrap/v1 design_only branch from the PNC-015 runtime-capable v2 native_runtime branch.
The schema draft discriminates payload schemas by artifact_kind and defines every artifact_kind payload under $defs.
The row-by-row handoff matrix below maps every required transition to schema_payload, producer, consumer, evidence_refs, and PlanUnit refs.
PlanCompile consumes the Executor-owned execution_unit_context schema by reference and does not redefine context fields.
`cmd.plan_compile.open_build` is a route/open or post-build reveal command with projected availability, disabled reason, and explicit receipt; it must not fabricate a PlanCompile success event or claim runtime activation while the branch is design_only.
Codex bootstrap external GUI-agent request is documented as a bootstrap artifact only, not a built Puppet Master setting.
Plan_To_Node_Compilation owns the Plan Compile side of the Plans-to-Code Handoff Matrix. Every transition from Planning Wizard Approve And Build approval and the PlanApproved handoff into PlanCompileRun state, then through PlanCompile, Executor intake, source-control preflight, dispatch, tests, Auditor verification, repair, promotion, graph completion, and certification must name row_id, transition, source_artifact, destination_artifact, producer, consumer, owner, validator, receipt, schema_payload, retry_route, rollback_route, user_escalation_condition, evidence_refs, and plan_unit_refs. For the current bootstrap/v1 matrix, Plan Compile source authority is the immutable ApprovedPlanPack plus frozen PlanUnit and acceptance-unit indexes; the Planning Wizard ledger remains source and reasoning lineage rather than executable Plan Compile authority. The shared `Plans/plans_to_code_handoff.schema.json` document keeps top-level `schema_id` at `pm.plans_to_code_handoff.v1`; within that stable document identity, the current bootstrap/v1 branch is the historical design_only contract with launch disabled, while PNC-015 owns the runtime-capable v2 native_runtime branch with runtime enablement evidence. PlanCompile and handoff rows consume the Executor-owned `execution_unit_context` contract only by reference through `Plans/Executor_Protocol.md` and `Plans/execution_unit_context.schema.json`; they must not define a local field list, omit schema_version from persisted context payloads, or persist secrets in context payloads. The schema draft in Plans/plans_to_code_handoff.schema.json records handoff_matrix, handoff_row, PlanCompileRun, stage card, compile worklist, NodeSeed candidate, NodeSeed review, WorkGraph draft, WorkNode request, compiler model routing, Codex work package, Codex external GUI-agent request, PlanCompile receipt, automated testing reports, test cases, test run receipts, visual evidence, source-control receipts, WorkNode dispatch/change/completion receipts, Auditor cycle and verification receipts, repair attempt receipts, legacy validation_pass_report compatibility aliases, model resolution receipts, and ExecutorIntakeReport shapes for the disabled design_only branch plus the runtime-aware native_runtime branch; neither branch creates runtime artifacts by itself. The PlanApproved handoff records the approval_cas_receipt, transactional outbox requirement, and deterministic idempotency_key over project_id, pack identity/version/hash, PlanningRun revision, topic map version, PlanUnit and acceptance-unit index hashes, testing policy hash, project-context snapshot hash, and final audit/closure hash so approval cannot create duplicate or stale PlanCompileRun state. The handoff matrix names Plans to WorkNodes as a design-only bridge. Do not expose this bridge as a built Puppet Master setting. Its schema boundary is the single `Plans/plans_to_code_handoff.schema.json` draft, whose `$defs` include a concrete strict payload definition for every `artifact_kind` enum value and whose top-level discriminator maps each `artifact_kind` to the matching `payload` schema, including `handoff_matrix`, `handoff_row`, `plan_compile_run`, `node_seed_candidate`, `worknode_request`, `test_capability_report`, `source_control_receipt`, `source_control_preflight_receipt`, `worknode_dispatch_receipt`, `auditor_cycle_report` and `validation_pass_report` while preserving source_artifact, destination_artifact, retry_route, rollback_route, and user_escalation_condition fields. Within that single schema_id=v1 draft, current bootstrap/v1 records use the historical design_only branch and runtime-capable v2 records use native_runtime only with runtime enablement evidence. H-001 through H-017 must remain present exactly once, and each row's schema_payload refs must resolve to concrete `$defs` or artifact_kind payloads. The historical per-artifact filename tokens `plan_compile_run.schema.json`, `node_seed_candidate.schema.json`, `worknode_request.schema.json`, and `test_capability_report.schema.json` are compatibility aliases for `$defs` in `Plans/plans_to_code_handoff.schema.json`, not separate schema files. dependency_anchors.text:
The live owner doc preserves every source atom listed in source_atom_ids without treating the ledger as canonical product prose.
Exact tokens, negative constraints, owner hints, and accepted corrections remain available to future audits through this PlanUnit.
No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, GoalRuns, implementation files, generated governance artifacts, or production build tasks are created by this compile.
Approve And Build records an approval CAS receipt and fails closed when final-review currentness inputs drift.
The PlanCompileRun identity is created or returned synchronously; projection identity reconciliation cannot be the source of run identity truth.
`cmd.runtime.approve` consumes canonical approval/currentness inputs, records UICommandResponse and approval/dispatch receipt refs, and emits only canonical runtime events or explicit receipts, never `runtime.command_applied`.
Approve And Build first validates a compare-and-swap approval boundary over the PlanningRun revision, topic map version, immutable pack identity, pack version, pack hash, project-context snapshot hash, PlanUnit index hash, acceptance-unit index hash, testing policy hash, and final audit/closure hash shown in final review. It then atomically writes the immutable pack, approval_cas_receipt, user approval receipt, and PlanApproved transactional-outbox event so approval cannot be committed without a recoverable downstream trigger. PlanApproved uses a deterministic idempotency key derived from project_id, pack_id, pack version, pack hash, and approval CAS inputs; duplicate delivery returns the existing PlanCompileRun rather than creating another run. In the finished-product native runtime contract, ordinary Approve And Build flow immediately creates or resumes exactly one PlanCompileRun and returns its identity synchronously before projection reconciliation; optional HITL checkpoints are policy exceptions, not the default. During the current bootstrap ledger-to-Plans lane, this remains product-runtime canon and does not launch PlanCompile. For broad stages the controller computes a bounded worklist and mandatory minimum parallel assignments, launches read-only subagents, records assignment and completion receipts, and rejects certification when required parallel work is absent. A required broad stage may reduce scope or block with a typed runtime-capability error, but it may not silently substitute one broad agent for mandatory parallel analysis or review. Activation requires all required active-scope WorkNodeRequests to be accepted together; optional work must be explicitly excluded or deferred before activation, and a mixed result cannot silently start a partial build. Orchestrator may show launch and provisioning progress before activation, but it marks the build running and exposes runnable WorkNodes only after the atomic activation commit and durable start receipt. Activation persists activation_pending, records_materialized, entrypoints_queued, start_event_pending, active, and cancelled_before_mutation states; retries resume idempotently, duplicate commands return the existing PlanCompileRun, and cancellation routes according to whether mutation began. Planning Wizard workflow and Auditor own AuditCycle, AuditFinding, RepairAttempt, AuditClosure, and CertificationReceipt records rather than Goal Runtime (DL-472, DL-478). The final audit controller must launch multiple bounded read-only specialist agents in parallel for distinct defect families, persist assignments and results, reduce findings, run bounded repairs, and re-audit until all findings are durably closed or a true typed blocker remains. Audit and repair subagents inspect, classify, compare, and propose; the Planning Run controller or assigned canonical artifact owner performs serialized writes, updates closures, and issues certification. Classify gaps as auto_resolvable, safe_default_with_assumption, defer_to_plan_compile, defer_to_worknode_system, requires_user_policy_decision, requires_user_risk_acceptance, requires_external_credential, or true infrastructure/runtime blocker.
